13 Core Data Engineering Concepts That Trip Up 80% of Candidates — Master These to Level Up.

Here’s a breakdown (with real interview-style thinking and how to actually practice):

1. Batch vs Streaming
Batch is cost-effective, but streaming delivers real-time freshness.

Miss the trade-off, and either your budget or your SLAs get wrecked.

Try this: Build a batch pipeline with Spark writing to S3 → then rebuild it using Kafka + Flink → compare cost, latency, and complexity.



2. Columnar Data Formats (Parquet, ORC)
Compression + column pruning = massive I/O savings.

Common mistake: Tiny Parquet files = slow queries + high overhead.

Try this: Run the same SQL over CSV and Parquet → EXPLAIN ANALYZE → compare scan time.



3. Partitioning & Clustering
Think beyond rows — partitioned folders reduce scan load.

But too many partitions? You’ve got a small file storm.

Drill: Partition logs by dt, cluster by user_id, and inspect Spark stage fan-out.



4. Schema Evolution
Data changes. Your pipelines must keep up.

Q: “How do you backfill a non-nullable column without breaking prod?”

Hands-on: Modify Avro schema in Confluent → test all compatibility modes.



5. Change Data Capture (CDC)
The best way to keep your warehouse in sync — minus the full refresh.

Warning: If you mismanage binlogs, expect duplicate or lost updates.

Challenge: Stream MySQL binlog via Debezium → Kafka → Postgres → check row-level accuracy.



6. Watermarks & Late Data
Time windows must close — but not before the data shows up.

Q: “What happens if a user's event arrives 3 hours late?”

Simulate: Use Flink’s allowedLateness, send late events, and observe state cleanup.



7. Idempotency
Retrying writes? They better not double your numbers.

Try: Write to Delta Lake using MERGE, replay Kafka topic, and validate totals.



8. Data Lineage & Metadata Tracking
If someone asks “why is this number off?” — you need answers.

Hands-on: Integrate OpenLineage with Airflow and trace one KPI’s full journey.



9. Workflow Orchestration
Airflow/Dagster gives you retriable, backfillable, observable DAGs.

Q: “How do you stop a daily job from running twice?”

Practice: Migrate cron to Airflow → configure depends_on_past & max_active_runs=1.



10. Incremental vs Full Loads
Full loads = simple but costly. Incremental loads = efficient but tricky.

Exercise: Convert a Redshift COPY from full S3 scan to incremental using manifests.


Pro tip: Don’t just memorize theory. Build. Break. Observe. Repeat.
